reporting_period: 09 Aug 2026 to 15 Aug 2026 (Certify removal window); Ops Notes week 2026-08-08 to 2026-08-15

quotes: QOWV Tote Transport — Totes Routed via Kansas (Weeks 3 and 4). Purpose. QOWV is Charm's aqueous bio-oil fraction, shipped from the Colorado production site to the Basco 6 injection site in Louisiana in intermediate bulk containers (IBC totes). Four totes injected in Week 3 (INJ-08-2026-W3) ... did not travel that route directly: they were trucked from Colorado to Charm's Kansas site on 2025-10-21, stored there, and later repositioned from Kansas to Louisiana.

Method. Truck transport is calculated as two terms. Vehicle embodied emissions are expressed per mile driven and are independent of load, so the miles of any given truck are apportioned between the batches sharing it, by each batch's share of the totes on board. Fuel use is expressed per tonne-mile and therefore needs no apportionment: each batch is charged its own cargo mass over the distance that cargo travelled.

Distances. Charm Colorado to Charm Kansas is 537 miles one way, and Charm Kansas to Basco 6 is 684 miles one way; each is evidenced by a filed route map. The via-Kansas route totals 1,221 miles against 1,201 miles for the direct route, 1.7 per cent longer.

Application — Week 3 (four totes, tags 118811, 118837, 118872, 118886): Colorado to Kansas (shipment #32/#33) 2 trucks, 34 totes aboard, 4 batch totes, share 4/34, miles 537x2, allocated 126.4. Kansas to Basco 6 (repositioning) 1 truck, 6 totes aboard, 4 batch totes, share 4/6, miles 684, allocated 456.0. Total allocated miles for the week therefore rise from 1,693.3, covering the 33 totes that travelled the direct route, to 2,275.7.

Which of the two trucks on the Colorado to Kansas shipment carried which tote was not recorded. This does not affect the result, because four totes out of 34 across two trucks allocates the same mileage as four out of 17 on one truck.
Carbon intensity is unaffected. Pyrolysis emissions for these totes remain keyed to the month in which the oil was produced, not to the route taken or to the week of injection.

QOWV Tote Transport — Vehicle Class Emission Factors. Correction. QOWV totes travel on a flatbed trailer, not in a tanker. Until this period the calculation applied tanker emission factors to both QOWV transport terms. Both now use the flatbed and non-tanker factors, which are the factors the equivalent WODO tote transport has always used: Fuel use, well to wheel — 0.1143 replaced by 0.1384 kg CO2e per tonne-mile (flatbed truck). Vehicle embodied — 0.23756 replaced by 0.19279 kg CO2e per mile (non-tanker truck).
Direction and effect. The correction ... increases reported QOWV transport emissions and so reduces the net removal, by approximately 0.9 tonnes CO2e for Week 3.
